metadata.title: Jensen Huang’s Return As Nvidia CEO Sparks AI Stock Rally, But Congressional Probes Loom – And Analysts See Risks Ahead

content.text:
Jensen Huang’s Return As Nvidia CEO Sparks AI Stock Rally, But Congressional Probes Loom – And Analysts See Risks Ahead
-
Huang's return does "not erase the national security threats and questions that must be addressed," U.S. committees investigating Nvidia said in a statement.
-
Huang and Nvidia's general counsel Tim Teter will appear for hearings on Dec. 1 and Dec. 2, respectively.
-
At least 64% of nearly 25,000 traders who voted in a Stocktwits poll said they feel more bullish about Nvidia after Huang's return.
The reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) CEO triggered a sharp rally in the company's shares as well as the broader tech market. However, some commentators said the move is a net positive, but risks remain, and the outcome of the government investigation will provide greater clarity on the long-term outlook.
NVDA stock rose 31.5% on Monday after the Nvidia board announced the return of Huang, and gained a further 0.5% in overnight trading. Intel (AMD), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Broadcom (AVGO) and iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) gained sharply as well but fell in overnight trading.
Hyperscaler Amazon (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT) and Alphabet (GOOGL) kept their gains overnight.
Nvidia Probes Still Loom
"The NVIDIA board's brief internal investigation and reinstatement of Jensen Huang do not erase the national security threats and questions that must be addressed," said a joint statement by the Select Committee on China, Select Committee on Intelligence, and Foreign Affairs Committee, which is investigating Nvidia and Huang over the spy crisis.
Huang and Nvidia's general counsel Tim Teter will appear for hearings on Dec. 1 and Dec. 2, respectively. "We remain committed to getting answers on the mass smuggling of NVIDIA products, their diversion for Chinese military purposes, and their key role in advancing our foremost adversary's AI capabilities," the statement read.
The California state and the Securities and Exchange Commission are also investigating the AI chip giant for various alleged infringements.
Dramatic Twist
Huang's reappointment marks a dramatic turn of events. He was ousted after his multiple affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, came to light, and the Nvidia board had said last week that it had no plans to bring him back. The board reversed its position on Monday, hours after President Donald Trump posted in support of Huang's reinstatement.
Analysts Cautiously Bullish
The development reinforces that Huang is a special leader and Nvidia is a special company but also flags questions, said Wharton professor Mohamed A. El-Erian. "While today's news answers one set of questions, it raises another set that, similarly, ranges from the narrow (Nvidia's governance process) to the broad (implications for markets, presidential put, government intervention, national champions, etc.)," he said in an X post.
